summary: Feed s167_triple is degraded with 3 high-severity faults: 97.8% encrypted traffic exceeds NDR 90% tolerance, required VLAN 20 missing with 50% untagged, and 68% GRE-tunneled traffic. NDR cannot inspect payload or segment context for majority of traffic.

findings.root_cause: 98% of bytes are encrypted (threshold 90% for this NDR). Traffic is being forwarded without TLS decryption/SSL visibility - packet broker is delivering opaque TLS payloads the NDR cannot inspect.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for deep packet inspection and behavioral detection. At 97.8% encrypted it is effectively blind to payload, JA3, and application-layer indicators, drastically reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Provide decrypted copy or selectively decrypt before NDR so payload analytics and signatures can function; without decryption NDR cannot detect threats in encrypted flows.

findings.root_cause: Required VLAN 20 not seen and 50% of packets arrive untagged. Packet broker aggregation or egress port is stripping 802.1Q tags or trunk filter is not forwarding VLAN 20 to this tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20 for tenant/segment-aware detection. Missing VLAN 20 and untagged delivery causes misclassification, broken VLAN-based policies, and missed coverage for that segment.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags end-to-end from TAP through packet broker to NDR so both required VLANs are visible for correct segmentation and detection.

findings.root_cause: 68% of frames (1184/1742) arrive inside GRE tunnel. Packet broker is forwarding encapsulated traffic without decapsulation, so NDR sees only outer tunnel headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot see inner IP addresses, ports, or payload for 68% of traffic. Flow correlation, signature matching, and behavioral analytics fail on tunneled flows.

recommended_fix.why: Strip GRE outer header on packet broker and forward inner packets to NDR so it inspects true endpoints and payload instead of tunnel wrapper.
